text:
olivia: heads-up — planning a staggered maintenance for eu-west3 GPU fleet next Tue 03:00-07:00 UTC. kernel + NV firmware patches. will do AZ-by-AZ drains, small capacity windows :calendar:

kai: got it. what's the planned stagger size?

olivia: aiming for 20% pod drain per AZ, sequential across 3 AZs (eu-west3-a/b/c). target rolling every 45m with 15m validation.

maria: +1 on stagger. pls confirm we keep a 10% reserved buffer for realtime customers (dedicated pools).

jonah: we should pre-warm a spare pool in each AZ to absorb traffic. provisioning 6 spare g4dn-like nodes per AZ. cost impact ~ $1.2k for the window.

olivia: budget acknowledged. product-ops can we surface to affected accounts?

product-ops: yes, we'll send a targeted notice to Dedicated and Private customers in eu-west3. include SLA impact and fallback guidance.

infra-bot: scheduled job created: maintenance/eu-west3-staggered-1758901234.kaniko

sre-oncall: list of validation checks we'll run after each AZ: 1) infra ping/latency to KV stores 2) rdma link check on GPU NICs 3) request path smoke tests to the hosted API 4) model-eviction/cold-start latency sample

kai: add a quick script to validate KV tail latency: `for host in $(cat eu-west3_hosts.txt); do curl -sS -m 2 http://$host:9090/health | jq .latency; done`

maria: note: if KV latency spikes >50ms we abort and roll back to previous kernel. must notify oncall ASAP.

jonah: for draining: use `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` then let autoscaler fill pre-warmed pool.

olivia: also plan to pin canary traffic to patched nodes for 10 minutes before moving rest of workload. canary percentage: 5% of requests routed via smart-routing to patched variant.

infra-bot: canary rule created: route tag=maintenance-canary weight=5% for model-family=gpt-medium

product-ops: customer-facing note draft: "Short rolling maintenance in eu-west3, minor latency blips possible, no expected data loss. Affected: hosted API + dedicated capacity in eu-west3. We recommend planning requests >5s with retry backoff."

olivia: QA: run embedding perf on 3 common models and generation tail-latency histogram. collect p50/p95/p99.

jonah: suggestion: temporarily increase batching window from 8ms to 12ms while an AZ is drained to cut token cost spike. but monitor p95 latency.

kai: agree but only for non-realtime queues. will apply a route label: `priority=low` -> batch=12ms.

maria: blockers? hardware team flagged a potential RDMA firmware mismatch on 2 racks in eu-west3-b. we should skip eu-west3-b until we validate.

olivia: thanks — adjust plan: start eu-west3-a then c, run extra RDMA validation for b, then schedule b on a follow-up window if needed.

sre-oncall: make sure runbooks updated: rollback steps, `kubectl uncordon`, how to reassign capacity pools, and who to call (network-hw oncall).

infra-bot: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/maintenance-staggered (created)

jonah: one more: ensure metrics around token-cost-per-request are captured; we may need to throttle low-priority embedding jobs.

olivia: ACK. i'll publish final schedule + runbook update by EOD. please flag any customer/eng teams with hard constraints.

maria: pinging storage team to confirm no maintenance overlap for objectstore snapshots in same window.

kai: reminder: update autoscaler threshold to avoid double-scaling while nodes drain (`scale-up-cooldown=300s`).

product-ops: I'll include rollback notice and a link to status page for live updates.

olivia: if no objections by EOD, we'll lock and create the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:

jonah: note for posterity: after previous kernel update we saw a 0.8% increase in p99 for gen models — track that delta closely.

infra-bot: maintenance/eu-west3-staggered-1758901234 scheduled for 2026-05-12T03:00:00Z

olivia: last message — if anyone will be OOO during window call it out now.

maria: i'll be oncall that night.

kai: i'll be available up to 04:30 UTC then remote.

sre-oncall: I'll take rotation for escalation.

olivia: perfect — thanks team.
